raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add opt-in FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM support for Qwen3.5, on top of [vLLM #55688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55688) at `50a923892d61`.
This is a stacked draft until #55688 lands. The final commit contains the GDN changes. Earlier commits belong to that dependency.
This PR adds the GDN adapter to the parent ReplaySSM lifecycle; it does not duplicate the parent Mamba2 implementation. It does not modify FlashInfer.

Related PRs #62004 and #64699 implement Triton standard decoding. #56466 prototypes Triton speculative decoding with prefix caching.
This PR instead integrates existing FlashInfer STP, MTP, and prefix-materialization APIs with the shared lifecycle in #55688.

## Claims

- Enable with `--use-replayssm` and `VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=flashinfer_replayssm`.
- Support draft lengths 0–7. Kernel widths are 1 for STP, 4 for draft lengths 1–3, and 8 for draft lengths 4–7.
- Preserve real scheduler lengths while padding kernel inputs with recurrent no-ops.
- Support cache modes `none` and `align`. Prefix caching requires `align`; `all` is unsupported.
- Preserve V1/V2 state ownership, canonical prefill, and aligned prefix materialization.

## Validation

The November 4 update preserves GDN support in the new NVIDIA Qwen3.5 implementation.
Its model-level cache sizing reuses the common implementation. Warmup commits extensible-cache memory before use.
V2 now derives replay classification from built GDN metadata. The parent tracker lifecycle and logical-column publication rules remain.

Focused checks ran through the saved `bash run-gdn-update-checks.sh`: 79 passed, seven skipped, and 583 deselected.
The existing GDN kernel file produced one pass and three CUDA skips. Warmup and kernel checks separately produced 12 passes and three CUDA skips.
Ruff, formatting, focused mypy, and CPU checks of the actual NVIDIA model sizing methods passed.
Commit hooks passed for upstream commit `8a65743946ea`.

Review found an incompatible adaptive-verification path: GPU-only query lengths differ from the CPU lengths used for GDN output placement.
The integration rejects that combination rather than adding a separate GPU indexing implementation.
A focused validator check confirmed that fixed-length MTP passes and adaptive verification raises the intended error. No new test cases were retained.

Current-revision GPU checks ran on OCI-JHB GB300 with `nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4` at `98915d837c4e`.
The four-prompt MTP3 comparison passed the existing top-five log-probability check. One of four prompts matched all token IDs exactly.
Both arms produced relevant responses. The other prompts differed in spacing or wording. This is not exact token parity or general quality evidence.
ReplaySSM selected all 36 GDN layers. Both STP prefix-cache smoke runs recorded four cache hits and 48 cached tokens with CUDA graphs enabled.

The measurements reuse the parent PR's workload and timing procedures.
They cover STP batch 256, natural MTP3 batches 256/512, prefix reuse, long-context serving, and full GSM8K quality.
Both arms use BF16 state because the current FlashInfer GDN adapter requires it. This differs from the [paper's FP32-state protocol](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.13778v1).
All four GSM8K cells completed. Each used TP2, eager execution, natural MTP5, and 1,319 five-shot questions.

| Cache mode | OFF correct | ON correct | OFF accuracy | ON accuracy | Cached tokens in each arm |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | 1,152 | 1,145 | 87.34% | 86.81% | 0 |
| align | 1,161 | 1,158 | 88.02% | 87.79% | 674,816 |

All four runs produced zero invalid answers. Both declared two-percentage-point accuracy-loss checks are **inconclusive**.
The no-prefix loss is 0.53 points, with a conservative paired 95% interval of -1.47 to +2.52 points.
The align loss is 0.23 points, with an interval of -1.68 to +2.14 points. These results do not establish quality parity.

The align pair uses `--prefix-match-unit 512 --block-size 512` in both arms.
The prompts share 673 tokens; checkpoint 512 lies inside that common prefix for every question.
An initial one-token-unit attempt recorded zero hits and is excluded from the prefix result.

Mean acceptance lengths were 4.574 OFF / 4.568 ON without caching and 4.578 / 4.575 with align caching.
Request durations were 70.76 / 142.99 seconds without caching and 67.34 / 145.24 seconds with align caching.
ReplaySSM was slower in both eager MTP5 evaluations. All 48 measurements are now complete; long-context results follow.

### Completed throughput measurements

All 32 paper-workload cells passed. Each rate is the arithmetic mean of two complete cell rates, with OFF/ON/ON/OFF ordering.
Runs use TP1, V2, CUDA graphs, and BF16 state. OFF selects `cuda`; ON selects `flashinfer_replayssm` with buffer length 16.
With default settings, STP dispatch uses packed Triton recurrence; MTP uses fused CUDA speculative decode.
The selector alone does not establish which STP kernel executed.
Aggregate throughput includes prefill and generation. Decode rate is the reciprocal of mean per-request TPOT.

| Cache | Workload | Batch | OFF aggregate TPS | ON aggregate TPS | ON/OFF | OFF decode TPS | ON decode TPS |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | STP | 256 | 12,643.64 | 12,457.74 | 0.9853 | 50.1788 | 52.1976 |
| none | Natural MTP3 | 256 | 16,032.86 | 14,701.11 | 0.9169 | 74.4961 | 100.1657 |
| none | Natural MTP3 | 512 | 16,066.94 | 15,582.41 | 0.9698 | 49.5917 | 56.4086 |
| align | STP | 256 | 12,462.02 | 12,553.09 | 1.0073 | 49.2748 | 49.7328 |
| align | Natural MTP3 | 256 | 16,508.81 | 20,369.70 | 1.2339 | 73.1716 | 95.1869 |
| align | Natural MTP3 | 512 | 14,664.54 | 25,795.29 | 1.7590 | 49.9042 | 60.8770 |

No-prefix runs show higher per-request decode rates but no aggregate throughput gain. MTP256 ON aggregate repetitions ranged from 13,307.63 to 16,094.59 TPS.
All no-prefix cells recorded zero preemptions. At batch 512, peak decode overlap was 449 OFF and 512 ON.

Prefix STP is close to parity. Both arms retained all 256 requests. Prefix MTP256 retained all 256 requests and 18,373 cached tokens in every cell.
The prefix MTP512 comparison includes different retention and admission. OFF retained zero cached requests, reached peak overlap 437, and had four/five preemptions.
ON retained all 512 requests and 36,649 tokens, reached peak overlap 512, and had zero preemptions.
The 1.7590x result therefore measures the complete serving configuration, not an isolated kernel gain.

| Cache | GSM8K batch | Standard aggregate TPS | Conventional MTP3 / standard | ReplaySSM MTP3 / standard |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none | 256 | 9,980.28 | 1.6065 | 1.4730 |
| none | 512 | 12,822.36 | 1.2530 | 1.2153 |
| align | 256 | 10,083.43 | 1.6372 | 2.0201 |
| align | 512 | 12,937.14 | 1.1335 | 1.9939 |

The standard references use the same prompts and 256-token output limit as MTP. The short-prompt STP workload generates 1,000 tokens per request.
All align standard references retained every cached request. Conventional MTP512 did not, so those ratios include that difference.

The hardware snapshot records GB300, driver 580.159.03, and a 1,400 W configured power limit; it does not measure power draw.
Python source is `8a65743946ea`; precompiled native components come from `f9db1756e9e6`.
The long-context STP comparison is complete. TP4, concurrency one, 51,200 initial tokens, and 20 turns of 2,048 input/1,024 output tokens.
Both arms disable prefix caching. Results average two repetitions in OFF/ON/ON/OFF order.

| Long STP metric | OFF | ON | ON / OFF |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate output tokens/s | 225.4570 | 128.2823 | 0.56899 |
| Reciprocal mean request TPOT, tokens/s | 291.0395 | 146.9919 | 0.50506 |
| Mean of per-run median TTFT, seconds | 1.05606 | 1.05579 | 0.99975 |

**This workload shows a substantial ReplaySSM regression.** All four runs produced 20,480 tokens with zero preemptions and zero prefix hits.
Startup logs confirm graph capture on all four ranks. Per-request graph replay was not traced.
Repeated outputs match exactly within each arm. Across arms, 18 of 20 turns match; the first difference occurs at turn 16, token 286.
This is performance evidence, not exact output parity.

Long-context MTP3 uses the same conversation and synthetic acceptance length 3.1151.

| Long MTP3 metric | OFF | ON | ON / OFF |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate output tokens/s | 379.9857 | 282.7779 | 0.74418 |
| Reciprocal mean request TPOT, tokens/s | 644.4661 | 398.2658 | 0.61798 |
| Mean of per-run median TTFT, seconds | 1.15786 | 1.08523 | 0.93727 |

ReplaySSM reduced aggregate throughput by 25.58%. Every run recorded zero hits/preemptions and observed synthetic acceptance length 3.11735.
Repeated outputs match within each arm. Across arms, 18 of 20 turns match; the first difference is turn 2, token 811.
These synthetic-acceptance results do not establish model quality.

The final MTP3 comparison keeps ReplaySSM enabled and changes prefix caching in OFF/ON/ON/OFF order.

| Metric | Prefix OFF | Prefix ON | ON / OFF |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate output tokens/s | 284.0952 | 279.7812 | 0.98482 |
| Reciprocal mean request TPOT, tokens/s | 398.6050 | 299.9919 | 0.75260 |
| Mean of per-run median TTFT, seconds | 1.07129 | 0.26519 | 0.24755 |

Prefix caching reduced time to first token by 75.25%, but aggregate throughput decreased 1.52% and decode rate decreased 24.74%.
Each enabled run reused 1,523,520 tokens, including 107,456 on the final turn. Disabled runs had zero hits.
All four runs had zero preemptions and identical output token arrays. Observed synthetic acceptance length was 3.11735 in every run.
The complete prefix group used a replacement allocation on the same node and four GPU UUIDs. Source, model, runtime, and providers stayed unchanged.

**All 48 cells passed execution checks. Quality remains statistically inconclusive, and the long-context replay comparisons show regressions.**

## Details

```text
request
  -> classify canonical prefill or replay
  -> pack replay rows and read ring views from cache pages
  -> publish accepted state through shared ReplaySSM lifecycle
  -> materialize aligned prefix checkpoints when required
```

Intermediate prompt chunks stay canonical. The V2 runner applies this rule before graph selection, including a `64 -> 1 -> 3` prompt schedule.

Required FlashInfer APIs are `gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush`, `gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush`, and `gdn_prefix_materialize` for aligned caching.
FlashInfer v0.7.3 at `775207deb340` supplies the MTP API and prefix materializer.
The exact STP module is absent from that release and main `eeed657f157b`. [STP PR #4974](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4974) is closed without merging.
**Remaining dependency: this adapter still requires the STP provider API.** Materialization is upstream through merged [#5073](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5073).
The measured runtime remains FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 with unchanged provider files from those PRs. This PR does not implement FlashInfer kernels.
Set `SGLANG_GDN_WY_STRIDED_QKV=1` before process startup.

The initial configuration requires BF16 activations/state, K=V=128, and supported Qwen3.5 architectures.
Pipeline parallelism, overlapping microbatches, adaptive verification, and KV connectors remain unsupported.
GDN kernel autotuning is not added by this PR.

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses shared lifecycle interfaces and existing FlashInfer APIs.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** CPU checks and all 48 measurement cells completed. Statistical quality checks remain inconclusive; performance regressions are reported above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable hooks passed; unrelated formatting was removed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Current evidence is separate from historical GPU results.

</details>

+### FlashInfer ReplaySSM
+
+FlashInfer ReplaySSM caches recent inputs to reduce full-state writes during Mamba2 decoding. It is disabled by default. Both Model Runners V1 and V2 support prefix caching with ReplaySSM, including MTP speculative decoding.
+
+This example enables ReplaySSM and prefix caching with three MTP draft tokens:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --max-model-len 12288 \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --mamba-backend flashinfer \
+    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
+    --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding \
+    --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
+    --use-replayssm \
+    --replayssm-buffer-len 16 \
+    --enable-prefix-caching \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
+```
+
+`--enable-prefix-caching` selects Mamba cache mode `align`. To use ReplaySSM without prefix caching, replace this flag with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. This selects mode `none`. To disable speculative decoding, remove `--speculative-config`.
+
+FlashInfer ReplaySSM has these limits:
+
+- `align` requires BF16 model inputs for its replay rings. The SSM state dtype is independent. The example uses FP16 state with stochastic rounding.
+- The logical replay buffer cannot exceed 16 tokens. For speculative decoding, it must contain at least `1 + num_speculative_tokens` tokens.
+- Pipeline parallelism, microbatching, and KV connectors are not supported.
+
+Prefix reuse still requires a shared prefix with a saved Mamba checkpoint. The matching rules for hybrid Mamba models above also apply.
+

+## Qwen3.5 GDN ReplaySSM
+
+GDN ReplaySSM stores recent recurrent inputs and reconstructs state from checkpoints.
+This optional FlashInfer backend is disabled by default. Enable it for Qwen3.5 with:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 SGLANG_GDN_WY_STRIDED_QKV=1 \
+VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=flashinfer_replayssm \
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
+    --dtype bfloat16 --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
+    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --use-replayssm \
+    --replayssm-buffer-len 16 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
+```
+
+This backend supports one to seven speculative tokens. It requires BF16 state and
+128-element key and value heads. Pipeline parallelism, microbatching, and KV
+connectors are unsupported. Adaptive verification is unsupported because GDN
+output indices require fixed verification lengths.
+Set `enable_adaptive_verification` to `false` in the speculative configuration.
+Prefix caching requires `--mamba-cache-mode align`.
+
+FlashInfer must provide `gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush` and
+`gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush`. Prefix caching also requires
+`gdn_prefix_materialize`. Check these APIs before use; a version number alone does
+not establish availability. This integration does not install missing kernels.

+def test_pack_replayssm_rows_preserves_tokens_and_masks_padding():
+    values = torch.tensor([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]])
+    packed = pack_replayssm_rows(
+        values, torch.tensor([0, 1, 3]), 4, padding_value=-torch.inf
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        packed.squeeze(-1),
+        torch.tensor(
+            [
+                [1.0, -torch.inf, -torch.inf, -torch.inf],
+                [2.0, 3.0, -torch.inf, -torch.inf],
+            ]
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _reference_gdn_step(
+    state,
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    a,
+    b,
+    A_log,
+    dt_bias,
+):
+    """FP32 recurrence using FlashInfer's effective BF16 gate constants."""
+    state = state.float().clone()
+    A_log = A_log.to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+    dt_bias = dt_bias.to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+    group_size = v.shape[1] // k.shape[1]
+    outputs = []
+    for token in range(q.shape[0]):
+        k_hv = F.normalize(k[token].float(), dim=-1).repeat_interleave(
+            group_size, dim=0
+        )
+        q_hv = F.normalize(q[token].float(), dim=-1).repeat_interleave(
+            group_size, dim=0
+        )
+        q_hv *= 1.0 / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1])
+        decay = -torch.exp(A_log) * F.softplus(a[token].float() + dt_bias)
+        beta = torch.sigmoid(b[token].float())
+        state *= torch.exp(decay)[:, None, None]
+        prediction = torch.einsum("hvk,hk->hv", state, k_hv)
+        update = (v[token].float() - prediction) * beta[:, None]
+        state += update[:, :, None] * k_hv[:, None, :]
+        outputs.append(torch.einsum("hvk,hk->hv", state, q_hv))
+    return torch.stack(outputs), state
+
+
+def _reconstruct_replayssm_state(
+    checkpoint,
+    k_cache,
+    u_cache,
+    g_cache,
+    committed,
+    ring_start,
+):
+    state = checkpoint.float().clone()
+    if committed == 0:
+        return state
+    rows = torch.tensor(
+        [(ring_start + offset) % k_cache.size(1) for offset in range(committed)],
+        dtype=torch.long,
+        device=checkpoint.device,
+    )
+    k_logical = k_cache.index_select(1, rows).float().repeat_interleave(2, dim=0)
+    u_logical = u_cache.index_select(1, rows).float()
+    g_logical = g_cache.index_select(1, rows).float()
+    final_g = g_logical[:, -1]
+    weights = torch.exp(final_g[:, None] - g_logical)
+    return torch.exp(final_g)[:, None, None] * state + torch.einsum(
+        "hpv,hpk->hvk", weights[:, :, None] * u_logical, k_logical
+    )
+

+            head_k_dim=128,

+        expected_output, _ = _reference_gdn_step(
+            accepted_state, q, k, v, a, b, A_log, dt_bias
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output.float(), expected_output, atol=8e-3, rtol=0)
+        _, accepted_state = _reference_gdn_step(
+            accepted_state,
+            q[:accepted],

+            dt_bias,

+        old_committed = int(committed[1].item())
+        if width == 1:

+        block_size=256,
+        shapes=tuple(tensor.shape[1:] for tensor in cache),
+        dtypes=tuple(tensor.dtype for tensor in cache),
+        mamba_cache_mode="none",
+    )
+    # Neighboring request rows provide valid canary IDs, making erroneous
+    # column reads deterministically corrupt another slot rather than crash.
+    block_tables = [
+        torch.full((256, 1), 3, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") for _ in range(2)

+    grouped = []

+        grouped.append(([mixer], spec, table))
+    context = ReplaySSMModelContext.create(grouped, max_num_reqs=1)
+    computed = 50_000
+    history_tokens = checkpoint_tokens = 0
+    # Reset a later prefill chunk, then reject, partially accept, and fully accept.
+    for step, accepted in enumerate([1] + [4, 1, 3, 2] * 5):
+        prefilling = step == 0
+        query_len = 4
+        if not prefilling:
+            if history_tokens - checkpoint_tokens + query_len > 16:
+                checkpoint_tokens = history_tokens
+            history_tokens += accepted
+        computed_after = computed + (query_len if prefilling else accepted)

+            query_metadata=_cuda_ints([0, query_len])

+def _stress_mamba_block_size(worker) -> int:

+
+    sizes = {
+        spec.block_size
+        for group in worker.model_runner.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups
+        for spec in iter_layer_specs(group.kv_cache_spec)
+        if isinstance(spec, MambaSpec)

+def _generate_with_preemption(llm, block_size: int):
+    """Preempt active requests, then complete decode across three cache blocks."""
+    engine = llm.llm_engine
+    # MTP excludes one trailing block from prefix hits. Keep three reusable
+    # blocks, plus that proof block and a decode margin.
+    max_tokens = 4 * block_size + 64
+    requests = {
+        "short": ("The capital of France is", 256),
+        "long": (
+            "Write a detailed history of mathematics, starting in antiquity.",
+            max_tokens,
+        ),
+    }
+    prompt_length = len(llm.get_tokenizer().encode(requests["long"][0]))
+    assert (
+        prompt_length + max_tokens + 8 <= engine.vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len
+    )
+    before = _metric_counts(llm)
+    # Queue both requests before scheduling either engine's initial batch.
+    llm.sleep(level=0, mode="keep")
+    try:
+        for request_id, (prompt, length) in requests.items():
+            engine.add_request(
+                request_id,
+                prompt,
+                SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=length, ignore_eos=True),
+            )
+    finally:
+        llm.wake_up(tags=["scheduling"])
+    latest = {}
+    preempted = False
+    observed_turnover = False
+    for _ in range(max_tokens + 1024):
+        for output in engine.step():
+            latest[output.request_id] = output
+        if len(latest) != len(requests):
+            continue
+        short, long = latest["short"], latest["long"]
+        if not preempted and len(long.outputs[0].token_ids) >= 32:
+            assert not short.finished and not long.finished
+            assert llm.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)
+            preempted = True
+        observed_turnover |= short.finished and not long.finished
+        if all(output.finished for output in latest.values()):
+            break
+    assert preempted and observed_turnover
+    assert all(output.finished for output in latest.values())
+    after = _metric_counts(llm)
+    assert after["vllm:num_preemptions"] - before["vllm:num_preemptions"] >= 2
+    for request_id, (_, length) in requests.items():
+        output = latest[request_id]
+        completion = output.outputs[0]
+        assert len(completion.token_ids) == length
+        assert completion.finish_reason == "length"
+        if request_id == "long":
+            prompt_len = len(output.prompt_token_ids)
+            crossed = (prompt_len + length - 1) // block_size - prompt_len // block_size
+            assert crossed >= 3, (prompt_len, length, block_size, crossed)
+            print(

+    )

+        "vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens", 0
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Adapters for FlashInfer's GDN ReplaySSM decode kernels."""
+
+import os
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from functools import cache
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import NULL_BLOCK_ID
+
+GDN_REPLAY_LOGICAL_WINDOW = 16
+
+
+@cache
+def _check_gdn_replayssm_environment() -> None:
+    if os.environ.get("SGLANG_GDN_WY_STRIDED_QKV") != "1":
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM requires "
+            "SGLANG_GDN_WY_STRIDED_QKV=1 before importing FlashInfer"
+        )
+
+
+@cache
+def _load_gdn_replayssm_mtp_kernel() -> Callable[..., torch.Tensor]:
+    _check_gdn_replayssm_environment()
+    try:
+        from flashinfer.gdn_kernels.gdn_decode_bf16_wy_ucache_flush import (
+            gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush,
+        )
+    except ImportError as e:
+        raise ImportError(
+            "FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM requires a compatible flashinfer-python "
+            "build exposing gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush"
+        ) from e
+    return gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush
+
+
+@cache
+def _load_gdn_replayssm_stp_kernel() -> Callable[..., torch.Tensor]:
+    _check_gdn_replayssm_environment()
+    try:
+        from flashinfer.gdn_kernels.gdn_decode_bf16_wy_ucache_stp import (
+            gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush,
+        )
+    except ImportError as e:
+        raise ImportError(
+            "FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM STP requires a compatible "
+            "flashinfer-python build exposing "
+            "gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush"
+        ) from e
+    return gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush
+
+
+def check_gdn_replayssm_dependencies(
+    executed_width: int, needs_materializer: bool
+) -> None:
+    """Check selected FlashInfer exports during GPU worker layer construction."""
+    if executed_width == 1:
+        loader = _load_gdn_replayssm_stp_kernel
+        api = "gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush"
+    elif executed_width in (4, 8):
+        loader = _load_gdn_replayssm_mtp_kernel
+        api = "gated_delta_rule_mtp_ucache_flush"
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported GDN ReplaySSM executed width: {executed_width}")
+    mode = f"executed width={executed_width}, cache mode=" + (
+        "align" if needs_materializer else "none"
+    )
+    try:
+        loader()
+    except ImportError as e:
+        raise ImportError(
+            f"FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM ({mode}) requires {api}: {e}"
+        ) from e
+    if needs_materializer:
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.ssu_dispatch import (
+            _load_gdn_replayssm_materialize,
+        )
+
+        try:
+            _load_gdn_replayssm_materialize()
+        except ImportError as e:
+            raise ImportError(
+                f"FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM ({mode}) requires "
+                f"gdn_prefix_materialize: {e}"
+            ) from e
+
+
+def pack_replayssm_rows(
+    values: torch.Tensor,
+    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    executed_query_width: int,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    padding_value: float = 0.0,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pack flattened ragged rows into fixed-width rows."""
+    num_rows = query_start_loc.numel() - 1
+    if num_rows == 0:
+        return values.new_empty((0, executed_query_width, *values.shape[1:]))
+    if values.shape[0] == 0:
+        raise ValueError("cannot pack non-empty ReplaySSM rows from an empty tensor")
+    if offsets is None:
+        offsets = torch.arange(
+            executed_query_width,
+            dtype=query_start_loc.dtype,
+            device=query_start_loc.device,
+        )
+    else:
+        offsets = offsets[:executed_query_width]
+    row_offsets = offsets.unsqueeze(0).expand(num_rows, -1)
+    query_lens = torch.diff(query_start_loc).unsqueeze(1)
+    valid = row_offsets < query_lens
+    source_indices = query_start_loc[:-1].unsqueeze(1) + row_offsets
+    source_indices = source_indices.clamp(max=max(values.shape[0] - 1, 0))
+    packed = values.index_select(0, source_indices.reshape(-1).long()).view(
+        num_rows, executed_query_width, *values.shape[1:]
+    )
+    mask = valid.reshape(num_rows, executed_query_width, *([1] * (values.dim() - 1)))
+    return packed.masked_fill(~mask, padding_value)
+
+
+def run_gdn_replayssm(
+    *,
+    mixed_qkv: torch.Tensor,
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    checkpoint_state: torch.Tensor,
+    replayssm_cache: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...],
+    ring_start: torch.Tensor,
+    num_committed: torch.Tensor,
+    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    output_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    executed_query_width: int,
+    num_k_heads: int,
+    num_v_heads: int,
+    head_k_dim: int,
+    head_v_dim: int,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    kernel: Callable[..., torch.Tensor] | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pack rows, invoke FlashInfer, and return only real-token outputs.
+
+    STP receives one real row per request. The adapter supplies FlashInfer's
+    caller-owned padded T=4 staging layout, while vLLM keeps cursor publication
+    model-wide so every layer observes the same pre-step cursor.
+    """
+    if executed_query_width not in (1, 4, 8):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM requires executed width 1, 4, or 8, got "
+            f"{executed_query_width}"
+        )
+    if len(replayssm_cache) != 3:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM requires exactly three auxiliary rings"
+        )
+    if mixed_qkv.dtype != torch.bfloat16 or checkpoint_state.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "FlashInfer GDN ReplaySSM requires bfloat16 inputs and checkpoint state"
+        )
+
+    # Native STP's public contract is T=1, but its serving fast path consumes a
+    # caller-owned zero-padded T=4 buffer. Packing a shared QKV allocation here
+    # preserves the common token stride required by block-strided cache pools.
+    packed_width = 4 if executed_query_width == 1 else executed_query_width
+    packed_qkv = pack_replayssm_rows(mixed_qkv, query_start_loc, packed_width, offsets)
+    # CuTe requires every input pointer to be 16-byte aligned. Packing the two
+    # gates together and splitting them can leave ``b`` at a small byte offset
+    # into the shared allocation when the local head count is not a multiple of
+    # eight. Give each gate its own aligned allocation instead.
+    # The MTP kernel advances every padded lane. Make those lanes exact
+    # recurrent no-ops: a=-inf gives zero decay after softplus(a + dt_bias),
+    # while zero q/k/v and b give a zero state update. STP has no ragged real
+    # rows, so only invalid graph-padding requests can be padded here; their
+    # negative state index skips the kernel CTA.
+    packed_a = pack_replayssm_rows(
+        a,
+        query_start_loc,
+        packed_width,
+        offsets,
+        padding_value=0.0 if executed_query_width == 1 else -torch.inf,
+    )
+    packed_b = pack_replayssm_rows(b, query_start_loc, packed_width, offsets)
+    local_k_dim = num_k_heads * head_k_dim
+    local_v_dim = num_v_heads * head_v_dim
+    q_flat, k_flat, v_flat = packed_qkv.split(
+        (local_k_dim, local_k_dim, local_v_dim), dim=-1
+    )
+    q = q_flat.view(packed_qkv.size(0), packed_width, num_k_heads, head_k_dim)
+    k = k_flat.view_as(q)
+    v = v_flat.view(packed_qkv.size(0), packed_width, num_v_heads, head_v_dim)
+    # vLLM reserves block zero for padding, while FlashInfer exits a null-row
+    # CTA only for a negative index. Gather trackers through the safe padding
+    # slot, then translate every non-live row to FlashInfer's -1 sentinel.
+    valid_slots = state_indices > NULL_BLOCK_ID
+    safe_slots = torch.where(valid_slots, state_indices, NULL_BLOCK_ID).long()
+    fi_state_indices = torch.where(valid_slots, state_indices, -1)
+    hist_len = num_committed.index_select(0, safe_slots).masked_fill(~valid_slots, 0)
+    cache_base = ring_start.index_select(0, safe_slots).masked_fill(~valid_slots, 0)
+    u_cache, k_cache, g_cache = replayssm_cache
+    output = torch.zeros(
+        packed_qkv.size(0),
+        executed_query_width,
+        num_v_heads,
+        head_v_dim,
+        dtype=mixed_qkv.dtype,
+        device=mixed_qkv.device,
+    )
+
+    if kernel is None:
+        kernel = (
+            _load_gdn_replayssm_stp_kernel()
+            if executed_query_width == 1
+            else _load_gdn_replayssm_mtp_kernel()
+        )
+    common_kwargs = dict(
+        # These are immutable model parameters. CuTe's DLPack bridge rejects
+        # tensors whose Parameter wrapper still advertises autograd tracking,
+        # even while vLLM executes under inference mode.
+        A_log=A_log.detach(),
+        a=packed_a,
+        dt_bias=dt_bias.detach(),
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        b=packed_b,
+        initial_state_source=checkpoint_state,
+        initial_state_indices=fi_state_indices,
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+        scale=head_k_dim**-0.5,
+        output=output,
+        k_cache=k_cache,
+        u_cache=u_cache,
+        g_cache=g_cache,
+        hist_len=hist_len,
+        cache_base=cache_base,
+    )
+    if executed_query_width == 1:
+        # The STP wrapper self-commits these gathered cursor copies. Do not
+        # scatter them into the pool here: subsequent GDN layers must consume
+        # the same pre-step values. The model-wide postprocess publishes the
+        # equivalent transition once after the target step completes.
+        kernel(
+            **common_kwargs,
+            flush_min=GDN_REPLAY_LOGICAL_WINDOW - 1,
+            prepadded=True,
+        )
+    else:
+        kernel(
+            **common_kwargs,
+            flush_min=GDN_REPLAY_LOGICAL_WINDOW + 1 - executed_query_width,
+            restart_hist_on_flush=False,
+        )
+    return output.flatten(0, 1).index_select(0, output_indices.long())
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "GDN_REPLAY_LOGICAL_WINDOW",
+    "check_gdn_replayssm_dependencies",
+    "pack_replayssm_rows",
+    "run_gdn_replayssm",
+]

+)

+def initialize_replayssm_ring_trackers(
+    kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> None:
+    """Allocate and bind one tracker pair per ReplaySSM cache group."""
+    for group in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups:
+        names = [
+            name
+            for name in group.layer_names
+            if isinstance(layer := forward_context.get(name), MambaBase)
+            and layer.use_replayssm
+        ]
+        if not names:
+            continue
+        layers = [forward_context[name] for name in names]
+        state = layers[0].kv_cache[0]
+        num_blocks, device = state.shape[0], state.device
+        trackers = (
+            layers[0]._replayssm_ring_start,
+            layers[0]._replayssm_prev_num_accepted,
+        )
+        # Extensible caches rebind after capture. Keep the captured addresses.
+        if all(
+            t.numel() >= num_blocks and t.device == device for t in trackers
+        ) and all(
+            layer._replayssm_ring_start is trackers[0]
+            and layer._replayssm_prev_num_accepted is trackers[1]
+            for layer in layers
+        ):
+            ring_start, num_committed = (t[:num_blocks] for t in trackers)
+        else:
+            ring_start = torch.zeros(num_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+            num_committed = torch.zeros_like(ring_start)
+        for layer in layers:
+            layer._replayssm_ring_start = ring_start
+            layer._replayssm_prev_num_accepted = num_committed
+            layer._plans_replayssm_decode = False
+        # Triton plans each decode step in the group's first executed layer.
+        planner = min(names, key=extract_layer_index)
+        forward_context[planner]._plans_replayssm_decode = True
+
+
+def get_replayssm_block_copy_tensors(
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """Include shared trackers in scheduler block copies alongside packed pages."""
+    tensors: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    for layer in forward_context.values():
+        if isinstance(layer, MambaBase) and layer.use_flashinfer_replayssm:
+            tensors.extend(
+                (layer._replayssm_ring_start, layer._replayssm_prev_num_accepted)
+            )
+    return tensors

+def _reinterpret_u64_as_i64(value: int) -> int:
+    """Preserve a uint64 pointer bit pattern in a torch.int64 tensor."""
+    return value if value < (1 << 63) else value - (1 << 64)
+

+@triton.jit
+def mamba_state_copy_boundary(
+    num_tokens_running_state,
+    new_num_computed,
+    block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Return the aligned Mamba state-copy decision and destination."""
+    aligned_new_computed = (new_num_computed // block_size) * block_size
+    needs_copy = aligned_new_computed >= num_tokens_running_state
+    accept_token_bias = aligned_new_computed - num_tokens_running_state
+    dest_block_idx = aligned_new_computed // block_size - 1
+    return needs_copy, accept_token_bias, dest_block_idx

+    idx_mapping,

+    dst_cols,
+    block_table_ptrs,
+    tracker_start_ptrs,
+    tracker_committed_ptrs,
+    block_table_strides,
+    PAD_SLOT_ID: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_IDX_MAPPING: tl.constexpr,

+    group_idx = tl.program_id(1)

+    tracker_committed = tl.load(tracker_committed_ptrs + group_idx).to(

+    dst_col = tl.load(dst_cols + req_idx, mask=valid_req, other=-1)

+        mask=valid_dst_col,
+        other=PAD_SLOT_ID,

+        mask=valid_src_col,
+        other=PAD_SLOT_ID,
